notes: All 15 exams were researched from live sources on 2026-11-17; every source URL below was fetched and its content extracted during this pass. (Environment quirk: the sandbox wipes /tmp between shell calls, so a handful of pages whose extracted text was lost were re-fetched once; fetch totals stayed within ~1-3 per exam.)

UPSC CSE GS and the two optionals: upsc.gov.in itself was unreachable from the sandbox (connection failure) and clearias.com / collegedunia.com returned 403, so BYJU'S mirrors were used: the HTML syllabus page for GS (Papers I-IV reproduced verbatim from the official notification; the area-level lines below are compressed by us from each paper's bullet text, keeping the syllabus's own area names) and BYJU'S CDN PDF copies of the official optional syllabi (PSIR and Anthropology), whose text is the official UPSC notification syllabus. All marked 'mirror'.

UGC NET: the netugc.com mirror was fetched first but found to carry the pre-2019 Paper-2/Paper-3 syllabus structure (stale; e.g. Political Science showed the old core-plus-elective layout), so it was NOT used. The eight subject syllabus PDFs were instead downloaded directly from the official UGC NET Bureau listing page on ugcnetonline.in (syllabus-new.php, the 'NTA_All_R_Syllabus' set - the June-2019 revised syllabus that remains in force for current cycles). All marked 'official'.

UGC NET History: the official PDF numbers units I-X without giving each unit a separate title; the unit lines below are compact descriptors taken from each unit's own opening phrases and content (e.g. 'Negotiating the Sources', 'From State to Empire', 'Colonial Economy' are the syllabus's own opening phrases).
UGC NET Psychology: the official syllabus states ten numbered sections (1-10) rather than 'Unit' labels; recorded as stated.
ugc-net-geography covers two separate official NET subjects: Geography (code 80) and Population Studies (code 15); both unit lists are recorded, the latter prefixed 'Population Studies'.

AP courses: apcentral.collegeboard.org URLs returned 404 to the sandbox, but apstudents.collegeboard.org (also an official College Board site) served the current course pages, and the units were taken verbatim from them. AP Psychology shows the 5-unit structure of the 2024-25 course revision; AP Human Geography shows the current unit naming (e.g. 'Agriculture and Rural Land-Use Patterns and Processes'); AP US Government's official slug is 'ap-united-states-government-and-politics' (the shorter 'ap-us-government-and-politics' form 404s).

CLAT: consortiumofnlus.ac.in (official) currently hosts only the CLAT-2027 press release (test on 6 Dec 2026; 'further details ... shall be notified in due course') and no syllabus page for 2027 (older-year paths like /clat-2026/clat.html 404). The five-section structure and the Quantitative Techniques elementary-maths topic list were therefore taken from current-cycle mirrors (Embibe and Wikipedia), which agree with each other and with the consortium's stable five-section description; the official press-release URL is cited as the anchor source and mirrors are marked 'mirror'.

Line count is 188 topic lines, above the ~55-80 target: unit-level fidelity (7 UGC NET subjects x 10 official units plus Population Studies, the AP unit lists, and the UPSC optionals' numbered topics) inevitably exceeds it. This mirrors the sibling physics ledger's approach (445 lines). UPSC GS, PSIR and Anthropology lines stay at the syllabus's own paper/numbered-topic level, not micro-bullets.

Search engines were unreliable from the sandbox (duckduckgo html endpoint failed; Bing SERPs returned irrelevant junk), so URL discovery was done by direct site navigation: link crawling of ugcnetonline.in, the BYJU'S syllabus page's own PDF links, and College Board's canonical course-page slugs.

topics: GS-I: Indian Heritage and Culture - salient aspects of art forms, literature and architecture from ancient to modern times
GS-I: Modern Indian History - from the mid-18th century, the Freedom Struggle, post-independence consolidation and reorganisation

GS-I: History of the World - events from the 18th century (industrial revolution, world wars, redrawal of national boundaries, colonisation, decolonisation, political philosophies such as communism, capitalism and socialism)

GS-I: Indian Society - salient features and diversity; role of women and women's organisations; population, poverty, urbanisation and their remedies; effects of globalisation; social empowerment, communalism, regionalism and secularism

GS-I: Geography of the World - salient features of the world's physical geography; distribution of key natural resources and location of primary, secondary and tertiary industries; important geophysical phenomena and changes in critical geographical features
GS-II: Constitution of India - historical underpinnings, evolution, features, amendments, significant provisions and basic structure

GS-II: Governance and Polity - functions and responsibilities of the Union and the States, federal structure and devolution; separation of powers; Parliament and State legislatures; Executive and Judiciary; statutory, regulatory and quasi-judicial bodies; e-governance; citizens' charters; role of civil services in a democracy

GS-II: Social Justice - government policies and interventions for development; development processes and the role of NGOs, SHGs, donors and other stakeholders; welfare schemes for vulnerable sections; social sector services relating to health, education and human resources; poverty and hunger

GS-II: International Relations - India and its neighbourhood; bilateral, regional and global groupings and agreements; effect of policies and politics of developed and developing countries and the Indian diaspora; important international institutions, agencies and fora

GS-III: Indian Economy and Economic Development - issues relating to planning, mobilisation of resources, growth, development and employment; inclusive growth; government budgeting; effects of liberalisation on the economy; infrastructure (energy, ports, roads, airports, railways); investment models

GS-III: Agriculture - major crops and cropping patterns, irrigation systems, storage, transport and marketing of agricultural produce, e-technology in the aid of farmers; direct and indirect farm subsidies and minimum support prices; Public Distribution System and food security; food processing and related industries; land reforms; economics of animal-rearing

GS-III: Science and Technology - developments and their applications and effects in everyday life; achievements of Indians in science and technology; indigenisation of technology; awareness in the fields of IT, space, computers, robotics, nanotechnology, biotechnology and intellectual property rights
GS-III: Environment and Disaster Management - conservation, environmental pollution and degradation, environmental impact assessment; disaster and disaster management

GS-III: Security - linkages between development and spread of extremism; role of external state and non-state actors in internal security challenges; communication networks, media and social networking sites in internal security, basics of cyber security; money-laundering and its prevention; border security and linkages of organised crime with terrorism; security forces and agencies and their mandate

GS-IV: Ethics, Integrity and Aptitude - ethics and the human interface; attitudes; aptitude and foundational values for civil service; emotional intelligence; contributions of moral thinkers and philosophers from India and the world; ethics in public administration; probity in governance (RTI, codes of ethics and conduct, citizen's charters); case studies
Paper-I (Political Theory and Indian Politics): Political Theory - meaning and approaches
Paper-I: Theories of the State - liberal, neo-liberal, Marxist, pluralist, post-colonial and feminist
Paper-I: Justice - conceptions of justice with special reference to Rawls's theory of justice and its communitarian critiques
Paper-I: Equality - social, political and economic; relationship between equality and freedom; affirmative action
Paper-I: Rights - meaning and theories; different kinds of rights; concept of human rights
Paper-I: Democracy - classical and contemporary theories; models of democracy (representative, participatory and deliberative)
Paper-I: Concept of Power - hegemony, ideology and legitimacy
Paper-I: Political Ideologies - liberalism, socialism, Marxism, fascism, Gandhism and feminism
Paper-I: Indian Political Thought - Dharamshastra, Arthashastra and Buddhist traditions; Sir Syed Ahmed Khan, Sri Aurobindo, M. K. Gandhi, B. R. Ambedkar, M. N. Roy
Paper-I: Western Political Thought - Plato, Aristotle, Machiavelli, Hobbes, Locke, J. S. Mill, Marx, Gramsci, Hannah Arendt
Paper-I: Indian Nationalism - political strategies of India's freedom struggle; perspectives on the Indian national movement
Paper-I: Making of the Indian Constitution - legacies of British rule; different social and political perspectives

Paper-I: Salient Features of the Indian Constitution - Preamble, Fundamental Rights and Duties, Directive Principles; parliamentary system and amendment procedures; judicial review and basic structure doctrine
Paper-I: Principal Organs of the Union and State Governments - envisaged role and actual working of the Executive, Legislature and the Courts
Paper-I: Grassroots Democracy - Panchayati Raj and Municipal Government; significance of the 73rd and 74th Amendments
Paper-I: Statutory Institutions and Commissions - Election Commission, CAG, Finance Commission, UPSC and the national commissions (SC, ST, Women, Human Rights, Minorities, Backward Classes)
Paper-I: Federalism - constitutional provisions; changing nature of centre-state relations; integrationist tendencies and regional aspirations; inter-state disputes

Paper-I: Planning and Economic Development - Nehruvian and Gandhian perspectives; role of planning and the public sector; Green Revolution, land reforms and agrarian relations; liberalisation and economic reforms
Paper-I: Caste, Religion and Ethnicity in Indian Politics
Paper-I: Party System - national and regional political parties and their ideological and social bases; coalition politics; pressure groups; trends in electoral behaviour
Paper-I: Social Movements - civil liberties and human rights movements; women's movements; environmentalist movements
Paper-II (Comparative Politics and International Relations): Comparative Politics - nature and major approaches; political economy and political sociology perspectives
Paper-II: State in Comparative Perspective - changing nature of the State in capitalist and socialist, advanced industrial and developing societies
Paper-II: Politics of Representation and Participation - political parties, pressure groups and social movements
Paper-II: Globalisation - responses from developed and developing societies
Paper-II: Approaches to the Study of International Relations - idealist, realist, Marxist, functionalist and systems theory
Paper-II: Key Concepts in International Relations - national interest, security and power; balance of power and deterrence; transnational actors and collective security
Paper-II: Changing International Political Order - rise of super powers, bipolarity, arms race and the cold war; Non-aligned Movement; collapse of the Soviet Union, unipolarity and American hegemony
Paper-II: Evolution of the International Economic System - from Brettonwoods to WTO; socialist economies and the CMEA; Third World demand for a new international economic order
Paper-II: United Nations - envisaged role and actual record; specialised UN agencies; need for UN reforms
Paper-II: Regionalisation of World Politics - EU, ASEAN, APEC, SAARC, NAFTA
Paper-II: Contemporary Global Concerns - democracy, human rights, environment, gender justice, terrorism, nuclear proliferation
Paper-II: Indian Foreign Policy - determinants and institutions of policy-making; continuity and change
Paper-II: India's Contribution to the Non-Aligned Movement
Paper-II: India and South Asia - SAARC and regional co-operation; India's 'Look East' policy; impediments to regional co-operation
Paper-II: India and the Global South - relations with Africa and Latin America; leadership role in NIEO and WTO negotiations
Paper-II: India and the Global Centres of Power - USA, EU, Japan, China and Russia
Paper-II: India and the UN System - role in UN peace-keeping; demand for a permanent seat in the Security Council
Paper-II: India and the Nuclear Question - changing perceptions and policy
Paper-II: Recent Developments in Indian Foreign Policy

Paper-I 1. Meaning, Scope and Development of Anthropology (relationships with other disciplines; main branches - social-cultural, biological, archaeological and linguistic anthropology; human evolution and emergence of man; characteristics of primates and fossil hominids; biological basis of life; principles of prehistoric archaeology and cultural evolution)

Paper-I 2. The Nature of Culture, Society, Marriage, Family and Kinship (ethnocentrism and cultural relativism; social groups and stratification; laws, types, functions and payments of marriage; types and functions of family; descent, descent groups and kinship terminology)

Paper-I 3. Economic Organization (formalist-substantivist debate; principles of production, distribution and exchange in hunting-gathering, fishing, pastoral, horticultural and agricultural communities; globalisation and indigenous economic systems)
Paper-I 4. Political Organization and Social Control (band, tribe, chiefdom, kingdom and state; power, authority and legitimacy; law and justice in simple societies)

Paper-I 5. Religion (anthropological approaches; monotheism and polytheism; sacred and profane; myths and rituals; animism, animatism, fetishism, naturism and totemism; religion, magic and science; magico-religious functionaries)

Paper-I 6. Anthropological Theories (classical evolutionism, diffusionism, functionalism, structural-functionalism, structuralism, culture and personality, neo-evolutionism, cultural materialism, symbolic and interpretive, cognitive theories, post-modernism)
Paper-I 7. Culture, Language and Communication (nature, origin and characteristics of language; verbal and non-verbal communication)
Paper-I 8. Research Methods in Anthropology (fieldwork tradition; tools of data collection; analysis, interpretation and presentation of data)

Paper-I 9. Human Genetics (methods and applications; Mendelian genetics in man; genetic polymorphism and selection; chromosomal aberrations; race and racism; ecological anthropology - bio-cultural adaptations; epidemiological anthropology)
Paper-I 10. Concept of Human Growth and Development (stages of growth; factors affecting growth; ageing and senescence; somatotypes; methodologies for growth studies)
Paper-I 11. Relevance of Menarche, Menopause and Other Bio-events to Fertility; Demographic Theories; Factors Influencing Fecundity, Fertility, Natality and Mortality

Paper-I 12. Applications of Anthropology (anthropology of sports, nutritional anthropology, design of defence and other equipment, forensic anthropology, applied human genetics - paternity diagnosis, genetic counselling, eugenics, DNA technology, serogenetics and cytogenetics)

Paper-II 1. Evolution of the Indian Culture and Civilization (prehistoric and protohistoric cultures; pre-Harappan, Harappan and post-Harappan; palaeo-anthropological evidences from India; ethno-archaeology in India)
Paper-II 2. Demographic Profile of India (ethnic and linguistic elements and their distribution; factors influencing the structure and growth of the Indian population)

Paper-II 3. Traditional Indian Social System and Caste (Varnashram, Purushartha, Karma, Rina and Rebirth; theories of the origin of the caste system; dominant caste and caste mobility; jajmani system; tribe-caste continuum; sacred complex; impact of Buddhism, Jainism, Islam and Christianity)
Paper-II 4. Emergence, Growth and Development of Anthropology in India (contributions of 18th-20th century scholar-administrators and of Indian anthropologists to tribal and caste studies)

Paper-II 5. Indian Village, Minorities and Socio-Cultural Change (Indian village as a social system; agrarian relations; impact of globalisation on villages; linguistic and religious minorities; Sanskritization, Westernization, Modernization; inter-play of little and great traditions; Panchayati Raj and social change; media and social change)

Paper-II 6. Tribal Situation in India (bio-genetic variability and socio-economic characteristics; problems of tribal communities - land alienation, poverty, indebtedness, literacy, employment, health and nutrition; impact of developmental projects, forest policy, urbanisation and industrialisation on tribals)

Paper-II 7. Exploitation and Deprivation of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes; constitutional safeguards; ethnicity and ethnic conflicts; regionalism and demand for autonomy; social change among tribes during colonial and post-independent India
Paper-II 8. Impact of Hinduism, Buddhism, Christianity, Islam and Other Religions on Tribal Societies; Tribe and Nation State (comparative study of tribal communities in India and other countries)

Paper-II 9. History of Administration of Tribal Areas, Tribal Policies and Programmes of Tribal Development (concept of PTGs; role of NGOs; role of anthropology in tribal and rural development; contributions to the understanding of regionalism, communalism and ethnic and political movements)

Unit I: Negotiating the Sources (archaeological, literary and foreign accounts; pastoralism and food production; Indus/Harappa Civilisation; Vedic and later Vedic periods; Mahajanapadas and second urbanisation)
Unit II: From State to Empire (rise of Magadha, Mauryan polity, society and economy, Asoka's Dhamma; post-Mauryan regional powers; Gupta-Vakataka age; Harsha)

Unit III: Emergence of Regional Kingdoms and Characteristics of Early Medieval India (kingdoms of the Deccan, South, East, West and North; state-formation debates; agrarian economy, trade and urbanisation; temple patronage; society, education and regional languages)
Unit IV: Sources and Political Developments of Medieval India (Delhi Sultanate - Ghorids to Lodis; Mughal Empire; later Mughals; Vijayanagara and the Bahmanis; rise of the Marathas)

Unit V: Administration and Economy of Medieval India (Sultanate, Mughal, Deccan and Maratha administration; frontier policies; agricultural production and irrigation; industries; trade and commerce; currency)
Unit VI: Society and Culture of Medieval India (Sufis; Bhakti movement; Sikh movement; social classification and position of women; education; fine arts; Indo-Islamic architecture)

Unit VII: Sources of Modern Indian History and Rise of British Power (European traders; establishment and expansion of British dominion; Revolt of 1857; administration of the Company and the Crown; constitutional changes 1909-1935)

Unit VIII: Colonial Economy and Indian Society in Transition (changing composition and direction of trade; commercialisation of agriculture; decline of industries; economic drain; famines and epidemics; the new education; Indian Renaissance; women's question; printing press and public opinion)

Unit IX: Rise of Indian Nationalism and India after Independence (birth of the Indian National Congress; early and assertive nationalists; Swadeshi and Swaraj; Gandhian mass movements; left wing politics; communal politics and partition; integration of states; constitution-making; planning and economic policies; linguistic reorganisation; foreign policy initiatives)

Unit X: Historical Method, Research, Methodology and Historiography (scope and importance of history; objectivity and bias; causation; research methodology and hypothesis; trends in historical research; Indian and western historiography; thesis writing and plagiarism)
